analysis_steps.goal: Make velocity-integrated moment-0 maps of isolated iCOM transitions

method.value: Integrate isolated transitions (no adjacent contamination or contamination below 3 sigma) over the full line profile in the ALCHEMI continuum-subtracted cubes; group maps by Eu range and overlay contours

evidence.quote: We then centred each spectrum at the local standard of rest velocity (LSRK) corresponding to the rest frequency of each transition used in this work before performing a Gaussian line fitting to the detected transitions.

evidence.quote: Due to the fact that we observe deviations from the fits in the RDs, it is clear that the derived $T_{\text{rot}}$ are not representative of the true gas temperature.

limitations_admitted.value: Two-component treatment assumes the warm compact component contributes negligibly to the cold extended one

limitations_admitted.value: Abundance study not performed (column densities only)

evidence.quote: An abundance study is beyond the scope of this paper.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only methanimine has an LVG treatment; other species' column densities rely on LTE rotational diagrams that the paper itself says are not representative of true gas conditions.
Splitting emission into 1.6'' and 0.12'' components is an assumption (pSSC size taken from literature) and the pSSC-scale column densities scale strongly with the assumed size.
No formal uncertainties on the correlations in the pair plots; p-value method unspecified.
Moment-0 maps and Gaussian fits depend on ALCHEMI line identifications partly by private communication.
The chemical-link and shock/heating interpretations are qualitative; no chemical modelling is done.

reproducibility.score_reason: Recipe for spectra extraction, rotational diagrams and LVG is described with key assumptions and numbers, but imaging is deferred to the ALCHEMI paper, the cubes are team products, and fitting details and line identification (private communication) are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The paper does not state that the processed ALCHEMI cubes are public, and the line identification used partly relies on private communication, so the recipe is not fully reproducible from the paper alone.
